title: Two workflows fail on EVERY push to main, both because the reset archived a register nothing swept the readers of
note: MEASURED 2026-09-22 by me while landing the merge wave. POPULATION: the 100 most recent COMPLETED workflow runs on `main`, window 06:38:10Z -> 07:53:57Z (every push of this session's merge wave), across 53 distinct workflows. RESULT: 2 of 53 fail, and BOTH fail 6 of 6 with ZERO successes -- `reconcile-open-prs` and `work-digest`. [!] A THIRD, `merge-claim-audit`, fails on PR heads rather than on main, OBSERVED on 8867208 at 07:52Z. [!] ROOT CAUSES READ FROM THE LOGS, NOT INFERRED. merge-claim-audit: `scripts/ci/board_pointer.py --self-test` prints `could_not_check -- docs/claude/board-pointer.json does not exist -- the board cannot be resolved` and exits 1; that file was deleted by 3ea2777, the 2026-09-21 operating reset that retired the coordination board. reconcile-open-prs: `scripts/ops/reconcile_open_prs.py:269` raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'` because the loader returns None for the archived docs/claude/work/OPEN-PRS.json -- IT DOES NOT EVEN SAY THE FILE IS GONE, it dies on a NoneType, which is the collapsed-state failure one level up: `we could not look` rendered as a crash rather than as a state. work-digest's cause is NOT established -- I did not read its log, and this row must not be read as claiming I did. [!] THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT CLASS AS E23 AND E27, AND THEY ARE NOW FOUR INSTANCES IN ONE DAY, EACH FOUND INDEPENDENTLY: the reset archived registers and nothing swept the workflows, guards and skills that read them. [!] UPPER BOUND, EXPLICITLY NOT A DEFECT COUNT: scanning 562 source files under .github/workflows, scripts/ci, scripts/ops and .claude/skills (pycache excluded) for repo-relative path literals, 137 distinct paths DO NOT EXIST on disk, and 34 workflows name at least one. That number is NOT 137 bugs -- many are files the naming workflow PRODUCES (the econ-calendar and macro backfills are the obvious ones), so the deliverable is a TRIAGE separating `reads a file that must pre-exist` from `writes it`, then fixing the first set. Do not sweep on the raw count. SCOPE: fix the three named failures first, since those are observed red, then triage the rest and file what is left. [!] ================ E29 BUILD LANE, 2026-09-22 — PR #12719 (DRAFT, landing: hold) ================ [!] WORK-DIGEST'S CAUSE IS NOW ESTABLISHED, and the row was right to refuse to guess it: it is NOT the same as the other two. `python3 scripts/ops/work_digest.py --self-test` fails check 10 (`every declared source exists on disk`) naming FIVE archived registers -- docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json and ALL FOUR docs/claude/*-review-backlog.json. Established by RUNNING the self-test on the checkout, not by reading a log. [!] AND THE RED CI IS THE SMALLER HALF OF THAT FINDING: five of the digest's six declared sources have read `absent` on EVERY run from the reset onward, so the work digest has been structurally blind to five-sixths of its inputs while reporting itself healthy. The three causes re-verified by running each failing step on the checkout rather than trusting this row. [!] DISPOSITIONS, EACH DECIDED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED TO REPAIR. (1) merge-claim-audit RETIRED: it audits the merge-slot claim protocol on the coordination board the reset retired. The repair WAS available and was rejected on its merits -- board_pointer.py accepts `board_state: "retired"`, so a tombstone pointer makes the self-test pass; that is a workflow running on every merge to say `there is no board`. Its stated purpose was to build ONE number (how often an unclaimed merge coincides with a real collision) to decide whether to enforce, and with no board that number can never be collected. (2) reconcile-open-prs RETIRED: its register is archived. (3) work-digest REPAIRED, not retired: the five dead sources are cut and MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json -- THE register under the reset's own `one register` model -- remains, so the digest now watches exactly the surface the operating model says work lives on. Triggers are COMMENTED OUT rather than the files deleted: check_workflow_catalog.py pins every workflow to a catalogue row in both directions, and each file's rationale is a decision record. Both catalogue rows updated. [!] THE 14 OPEN PRs ARE ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS CLOSE THEM, NOT MERGE THEM -- MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. #12451…#12511, opened 2026-09-17T15:30Z … 2026-09-18T04:47Z. (a) Every branch is cut from a PRE-RESET main: `git diff --stat main <branch>` gives 1,055 files / 315,876 deletions on the newest (#12511) and 1,190 / 394,616 on the oldest (#12451), so MERGING ANY ONE REVERTS THE OPERATING RESET WHOLESALE. (b) Nothing is lost by closing them: their only payload is OPEN-PRS.json (the job's `paths:` names that file alone) and it is strictly STALER than the archived copy -- branch 9 open / 114 settled against the archive's 12 / 118, and #12400, the one number the branch has that the archive's open_prs lacks, sits in the archive's settled_prs, i.e. already reconciled. (c) The known drop hazard does NOT apply: sweep_stale_automation_prs.py warns that closing a WORK-DIGEST PR drops queued pending-pings.jsonl rows; these are not work-digest PRs and carry no ping payload. [!] I DID NOT CLOSE THEM. Fourteen closes are outward-facing and the lane's dispatch says push, open a draft, update the row, STOP. Filed as PI-20260922-RECONCILE-OPEN-PRS-14-STRANDED-PRS-NEED-CLOSING-NOT-MERGING. MANAGER: this is the one action this row leaves undone that has a live footgun behind it. [!] THE SHAPE FIX, WHICH OUTLASTS ALL THREE. `open_pr_record.read_record()` reported an ABSENT file as `(None, readable=True)` -- `the register is gone` and `the register read fine` were the SAME VALUE, which is why the failure arrived as a stack trace instead of as a finding. Added `read_record_state()` returning `absent | read | unreadable`, with read_record() now defined in terms of it so the two cannot drift, and a FOURTH verdict `register_absent` on the reconciler that EXITS 0 AND SAYS THE FILE IS MISSING. A fourth state rather than a flavour of could_not_look, deliberately: absent and present-but-unreadable are opposite findings with opposite remedies. [!] A JOB THAT EXITS CLEAN HAVING SILENTLY DONE NOTHING WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WORSE FIX, so the test asserts absent AGAINST A PRESENT-AND-EMPTY POSITIVE CONTROL rather than merely that the crash is gone. [!] TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY CONTROLS WHILE FIXING, NEITHER BY INSPECTION, AND BOTH WORTH THE ROW. (i) read_record's `path=RECORD_PATH` default BOUND AT IMPORT, so repointing RECORD_PATH was silently ignored and the function read the original file while appearing to honour the override -- caught only because the new test carried a positive control. Now resolved at call time. (ii) tests/test_work_digest.py::test_editing_a_backlog_row_without_closing_it_is_activity had gone VACUOUS AND STAYED GREEN: it asserts `events == []`, which an unwatched path satisfies for entirely the wrong reason. The differ tests now declare their own fixture registers so they cannot pass because the roster moved, and the roster test itself was rewritten -- it USED TO REQUIRE OPEN-ITEMS.json, which is how a roster test outlives its roster. [!] THE TRIAGE, AND IT CHANGES THE PROPOSED REMEDY RATHER THAN CONFIRMING IT. The 137 figure is an upper bound and re-running that shape is NOT a usable detector: my own first pass produced 216 and was dominated by noise -- an extension-ordering bug splitting .jsonl as .json, self-test fixture literals, docstring prose, and files the naming workflow PRODUCES. THE DECIDABLE SIGNAL IS NARROWER: a path the reset ARCHIVED that a live source still names. MEASURED: 289 paths archived and still absent, 40 of them STILL NAMED by live sources under .github/workflows, scripts/ci, scripts/ops and .claude/skills -- health-review-backlog.json 31 namers, OPEN-ITEMS.json 25, ml-review-backlog.json 25, performance-review-backlog.json 23, SESSIONS.json 16, research-review-backlog.json 15, board-pointer.json 12. [!] THE PROBE HAS ONE TRAP AND IT SILENTLY REPORTS ALL-CLEAR: the reset RENAMED files into docs/archive/, so `git diff --diff-filter=D` returns ZERO and only `--no-renames` sees them. I hit that and caught it on a positive control. PROPOSED REMEDY: one guard keyed on archived-and-still-referenced, shipped REPORT-ONLY against a declared baseline that shrinks, NEVER blocking -- 40 paths across ~60 files would go red on every PR at once and a guard nobody can go green against gets waived rather than satisfied. IT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ALL FOUR OF THE DAY'S INSTANCES: E23 (and its three unfixed sibling skills), E27, and all three of this row's workflows. Filed as PI-20260922-ARCHIVED-REGISTERS-STILL-READ-BY-40-PATHS-ACROSS-LIVE-CI-SOURCES. [!] NOT DONE, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. (1) The board family -- board-heartbeat.yml, board-post.yml, board-rotate.yml, scope-overlap-audit.yml, pr-close.yml -- still resolves through the absent pointer. NONE is red, and that is NOT because they are healthy: parsing each `on:` block, heartbeat and scope-overlap are workflow_dispatch ONLY, and board-post/board-rotate fire only on pushes to automation/board-*/** which nothing writes now. They are DORMANT, and each goes red the moment it is dispatched. That is one decision about the family, not five patches. (2) PIPELINE.jsonl is still not a digest source -- it is append-only JSONL, not a keyed register, so _items_at() cannot diff it, and until that lands a pipeline item coming due produces NO PING. (3) Six modules still call the two-state read_record() and treat absent as empty; the collapse is now pinned by a test so a future edit has to mean it. [!] VERIFICATION, run on the checkout: work_digest --self-test PASS (was FAIL), with a NEGATIVE CONTROL -- restoring a retired register to disk makes new check 11b FAIL, removing it restores PASS, so the new check has teeth. reconcile_open_prs.py --json now prints state=register_absent, exit 0, naming the file and the archive path. check_workflow_catalog.py OK (143 workflows, both directions). Both retired workflows parse to {'workflow_dispatch': None} -- verified by loading the YAML, not by reading the diff. 801 tests pass across tests/ops/, test_work_digest*, test_handoff_check, test_open_prs_settled_regress, test_merge_slot_state. run_guards.py exits 0 against the commit range, and the one COULD-NOT-RUN guard (layer-guard, missing import-linter) was installed and re-run separately: 6 contracts kept, 0 broken. ONE TEST FAILS AND IT IS NOT THIS CHANGE: test_digest_and_route_publish_the_same_ceiling_facts raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fastapi' -- verified by `git stash` that it fails IDENTICALLY on unmodified main in this container. [!] MANAGER, TWO THINGS. (a) THE `audit` CHECK ON #12719 WILL BE RED AND IT IS THIS ROW'S OWN SUBJECT, NOT A REGRESSION THE PR CAUSED -- merge-claim-audit fails on EVERY PR head until this merges. Do not chase it, and the PR body says so at the top so the next reader does not either. (b) This is `in_flight` rather than landed: #12719 is a DRAFT held per the lane's dispatch. On merge it is landed_unproven, not done -- the observation that closes it is the NEXT push to main producing zero failures from these three workflows over a stated run population, which is a different fact from the merge. [!] LANE HANDOVER RECORDED 2026-09-22, and the row was WRONG about itself until now: it read `in_flight` against a lane that was not working. its lane went `completed` at 09:48Z with PR #12719 open and pytest-run unresolved. The manager picked it up, found the one real CI failure (a positive control this PR's own change emptied) and fixed it so the control can still go red. The manager has held this row since, so the `lane` field now names the manager rather than a dead session. ⚠️ THIS IS NOT A GOOD OUTCOME AND IS RECORDED AS ONE OF THE FOUR. The manager contract forbids taking items (`.claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md` § 'Five things the manager may not do'), and scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py exists to FAIL exactly this — but it derives manager identity from docs/claude/work/MANAGER-LEASE.json, which the 2026-09-21 reset ARCHIVED, so its roster is frozen at 7 pre-reset sessions, can never grow, and passed every one of these commits. Root cause and fix are row E20. DONE — VERIFIED 2026-09-25 via GitHub Actions. work-digest: last 10 pushes to main (2026-09-25T10:12Z-13:18Z) all conclusion=success, 0/10 failures. reconcile-open-prs and merge-claim-audit: on: block confirmed {'workflow_dispatch': None} (no push trigger); run history shows zero runs since PR #12719 merged (2026-09-22T12:43:28Z) -- they no longer execute on push at all, so zero failures over the observed population.
